items.title: 4 smallcaps with up to 332% PAT growth just surged 170%: Can the outperformance continue?
items.description: Smallcap stocks led Nifty-500 earnings growth in 1QFY27, with the Nifty Smallcap-250 reporting 35% YoY growth. While strong earnings, domestic inflows and themes such as power continue to support the rally, elevated valuations and narrowing market breadth highlight the need for selective investing.

items.title: Nvidia investors beware: Firm flags 2 risks after better-than-expected Q2 earnings
items.description: Nvidia’s AI boom remains strong, but rising memory costs and growing debt are emerging as key risks. The chipmaker expects gross margins to bottom at 71–72% in Q4 FY27, while rising debt could pressure its financial condition and cash flows.

items.title: ICICI Prudential AMC shares decline 5% as promoter plans 2% stake sale
items.description: ICICI Prudential AMC promoter Prudential Corporation plans to sell up to 2% stake, worth over Rs 3,185 crore, to meet minimum public shareholding requirements. The sale will reduce promoter holding to 85.6%. Shares of ICICI Prudential AMC have gained over 22% in 2026, while Q1 net profit rose 23% year-on-year to Rs 965 crore.

items.title: India equity outlook cut again as foreign funds seek value elsewhere in Asia
items.description: Forecasts suggest that by mid-2027, Indian equity markets may be trading lower compared to the beginning of 2026. This trend is driven by foreign investors shifting their focus to more promising Asian markets that offer better value and opportunities in AI. Although overseas investors have sold off considerable amounts of Indian stocks this year, domestic investors continue to back the market with systematic investment strategies.

items.title: Stock split alert! Last day to buy 2 multibagger microcap stocks which rallied up to 540% in a year
items.description: According to SEBI's T+1 settlement cycle, investors must buy a company's shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action. Accordingly, today is the last opportunity for investors to buy the shares so that they are credited to their accounts by Friday, making them eligible for the stock split.

items.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy Paras Defence, MCX, 34 other stocks for payouts. Do you own any?
items.description: This Friday marks the record date for dividend distributions from thirty-three companies, necessitating investors to buy shares today for eligibility. Included in this round of announcements are prominent firms such as Paras Defence and MCX. Notably, Honasa Consumer is celebrating its first dividend payout, bringing joy to its shareholders. Moreover, Protean e-Gov Technologies will also provide its planned dividend payouts.

items.title: PNB Housing outshines peers on strong loan growth
items.description: PNB Housing Finance shares have seen significant gains this year.  The company is focusing on affordable and emerging housing segments.  This strategic shift aims to improve its valuation and return ratios.  Disbursements and net profit are expected to grow robustly in coming years.  Stable asset quality and new financing initiatives support future growth.

items.title: Stocks in news: Tata Power, Jio Financial Services, Bharat Electronics and Hindustan Copper
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced minimal fluctuations on Wednesday, resulting in a lower close for the Nifty50. Although technical signals point to potential bearish trends, the overall outlook stays optimistic. Focus is directed towards Tata Power, which plans to challenge a recent court verdict, and Jio Financial Services, citing notable asset increases. Additionally, companies like Bharat Electronics and Hindustan Copper are navigating their own corporate maneuvers and regulatory matters.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks traded range-bound as Nifty fell below 24,300. Brent crude oil prices cooling provided some investor sentiment support. Geopolitical uncertainties kept market participants cautious during Wednesday's session. Analysts expect Nifty to consolidate within a broad range of 24,000-24,700. Foreign portfolio investors and domestic institutional investors were net buyers of shares.

items.title: Lenders may turn to OFCB route to raise more funds abroad
items.description: Indian banks are now shifting focus towards borrowing in overseas foreign currencies to meet their fundraising requirements. This strategic pivot comes in light of an advanced deadline on August 31 that altered original plans tied to deposit-linked fundraising. With the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) moving the timeline forward, many lenders have revised their bond issuance approaches.

items.title: Stock Radar: Narayana Hrudayalaya stock showing signs of bottoming out; time to buy?
items.description: Narayana Hrudayalaya stock has recovered after testing crucial support levels recently.  The stock is now trading above several moving averages, indicating positive momentum.  Experts suggest buying opportunities for short-term traders with a target of Rs 1975.

items.title: GAIL opposes IGX platform for LNG terminal capacity booking
items.description: India's top gas marketer GAIL opposes a new platform for booking LNG terminal capacity. GAIL states this platform will add costs for consumers without significant value. The company believes existing frameworks do not require a separate booking platform. High global LNG prices already pressure downstream natural gas consumers. Much of India's LNG regasification capacity remains underutilised currently.

items.title: Shifting Gears: PSBs borrow more to cater to credit demand as deposits lag
items.description: Public sector banks are borrowing more to fund lending expansion. Deposits are not keeping pace with credit growth for these banks. Private banks show stronger deposit growth and are gaining market share. This trend raises concerns about funding sustainability for state-owned lenders. Abundant system liquidity currently cushions the impact of these shifts.

items.title: Fire insurance premiums fall 28% in Q1 amid deep discounting
items.description: Fire insurance premiums dropped significantly in the first four months of the financial year. Aggressive discounting on large industrial risks pressured insurers competing for corporate accounts. The regulator received complaints of steep discounts, raising financial health concerns. Major insurers like New India Assurance and ICICI Lombard saw premium reductions. Pricing for industrial fire risks must now follow sound actuarial principles.

items.title: Tata Power loses challenge to $490 million arbitration award
items.description: Tata Power's challenge to a $490 million arbitration award was rejected by Singapore's court.  The court upheld damages awarded to Kleros Capital Partners regarding a Russian coal asset bid.  Disagreements over leadership and ownership soured the partnership in 2015.  Kleros alleged Tata Power misused confidential information and acted in bad faith.  The company must now pay Kleros' legal costs, which are yet to be determined.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A top private bank for a 3.95% upmove, a mid-cap auto components stock for gain of 5%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey clarifies on CAS changes after big Sensex expiry-day swing
items.description: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator has no plans to change the Closing Auction Session despite sharp expiry-day swings. Sebi expects participation and understanding to improve, while monitoring liquidity concerns and alleged manipulation. NSE IPO approval is also nearing.

items.title: Solar Industries among 5 stocks hitting 52-week highs; surge up to 22% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex declined 539 points to end the session at 76,933 on Thursday. However, the broader market continued to show strength, with five stocks from the BSE 200 Index hitting fresh 52-week highs, marking their highest levels in the past year. A 52-week high is widely viewed as a bullish technical signal, indicating strong investor interest and improving market sentiment, while suggesting the possibility of further upward momentum.

items.title: Calcutta Stock Exchange seeks Sebi nod for trading comeback
items.description: The 118-year-old Calcutta Stock Exchange is seeking Sebi guidance on reviving equity trading through interoperability or a new clearing corporation. The bourse is evaluating regulatory compliance options, with interoperability via NSE or BSE potentially offering a faster route.

items.title: Happiest Minds Technologies shares fall 6% as reports suggest ITC Infotech may buy promoter stake
items.description: Happiest Minds Technologies shares fell 6.16% after reports that ITC Infotech may acquire a 22% promoter stake. The stock settled at Rs 420.25, while investors weighed the potential transaction against the company’s recent profit and revenue growth.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: Sebi proposes scrapping merchant banker requirement rule for small-ticket debt via private placement
items.description: Sebi has put forth a proposal to exempt small-value debt issuances from the requirement of appointing merchant bankers. This initiative is designed to lower compliance costs and foster market growth for listed companies. To qualify, issuers must be regulated and have been listed for a minimum of one year, along with providing an auditor’s certificate to confirm no recent defaults.

items.title: Monthly Expiry shock: Did CAS fail its biggest test after Sensex loses 2,000 points in 6 minutes?
items.description: The Sensex witnessed a sharp late-session swing of over 2,000 points in six minutes on Thursday, raising fresh questions about the Closing Auction Session (CAS) on its first monthly derivatives expiry. The Nifty also ended lower as thin auction-window liquidity amplified volatility and drew renewed regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Market wrap: Adani Enterprises, Kotak Mahindra Bank, HDFC Bank, M&M top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian equity markets closed lower on Thursday, with the Sensex falling 539 points and the Nifty declining 117 points as selling intensified late in the session. Adani Enterprises and Kotak Mahindra Bank led Nifty gainers, while Hindalco, HDFC Bank and M&M emerged among the biggest losers.

items.title: India Inc’s revenue growth to moderate to 13-15% in Q2 FY27; margins under pressure: ICRA
items.description: India Inc’s revenue growth is expected to moderate to 13-15% in Q2 FY27 from 21.3% in Q1, ICRA said. Higher input costs could squeeze margins, while domestic consumption supports growth and weak global demand pressures export-oriented sectors.

items.title: Sensex sharply tumbles 500 points on first monthly expiry after CAS, Nifty closes below 24,100. What lies ahead?
items.description: Indian equities fell sharply on Thursday, erasing gains during the first monthly expiry under the new closing auction session. Sensex dropped 539 points, or 0.7%, while Nifty declined 117 points, or 0.48%. HDFC Bank and NTPC led losses, while Kotak Mahindra Bank, ICICI Bank and Tech Mahindra gained.

items.title: 13 midcap firms deliver over 25% profit growth for two straight quarters; shares surge up to 118%
items.description: Companies that report more than 25% YoY profit growth for two consecutive quarters signal strong and consistent earnings momentum. An ETMarkets analysis found that around 37 BSE midcap stocks posted over 25% YoY profit growth in both the March 2026 and June 2026 quarters.Of these, 22 stocks delivered double-digit returns over the past year. We highlight 13 midcap stocks that gained between 40% and 118% in one year, backed by strong profit growth over the last two quarters. Consistent earnings growth can improve a company’s cash-generating capacity, support future expansion and boost investor confidence. However, investors should also assess whether the growth is driven by core business operations or by one-off gains, tax benefits or other exceptional items. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: HDFC Bank shares fall 2% to fresh 52-week low, tumble 30% in 10 months. What lies ahead?
items.description: HDFC Bank shares fell to a fresh 52-week low after a US investor filed a securities fraud class-action lawsuit against the bank and two senior executives. HDFC Bank called the allegations meritless and said it would defend the case vigorously, adding to recent concerns weighing on the stock.

items.title: Do long-term investors need some unconventional thinking? 5 large-caps from different sectors with upside potential of up to 25%
items.description: It is rare for bulls and bears to agree on anything. At this juncture, however, they seem to agree on one point: That the Indian stock market is experiencing rather unconventional times. Why so? Because some of the best wealth-creating companies are quoting at valuations that are lower as compared to the past. At the same time, companies that have just got listed are quoting at valuations that are far above the conventional range.

items.title: Goldman Sachs says Britannia could see biggest cost impact as sugar prices continue to soar
items.description: Rising sugar prices are raising concerns over higher input costs for consumer companies, with Goldman Sachs identifying Britannia Industries as the most exposed among companies it covers. Nestle India and Varun Beverages could also face pressure. Tight global supplies, festive demand and adverse weather conditions are driving the commodity’s sharp rally.

items.title: Systematix initiates coverage on Timex Group India with Buy rating. Check target price
items.description: Systematix has initiated coverage on Timex Group India with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 820, implying around 30% upside. The brokerage expects strong growth through FY29, with revenue, EBITDA and adjusted PAT projected to grow at CAGRs of 29.1%, 37.3% and 40.5%, respectively, supported by premiumisation, margin expansion and strong cash generation.
